summary: The candidate follows from the supplied accepted block-layer bound with no mathematical errors or gaps. The block laws are uniform on the stated endpoint-fixed supports and invariant under reflection about their original centers, including singleton and endpoint layers. Their reciprocal second moments and averages factor exactly under the original conditional product probabilities. Reflection gives at least one-half of each law in every containing closed ambient halfspace, and Cauchy-Schwarz therefore gives the stated one-quarter factor. Summing against the original center weights produces the squared cell probabilities; their finite-sum bound proves the first two inequalities. Both dimension cases in the binomial estimate establish the last constant with the correct inequality directions. Nonempty profiles, arbitrary finite tilts, arbitrary allowed profile sets, weight rescaling, and the budget applications are all covered by the stated hypotheses.
